speaker: Head Coach
quote_text:
You're not interested in that. You're not  interested in all of that. Seven. And the other  
one? Two on hand over. Still 2-1. So they go into  extra time. Yep. What satisfaction do you take  
from coming away with a point or is the feeling  more about the two points that got away and the  
chances that got away tonight? The last thing.  The only reason why we could be happy with a 2-2  
was that they got the last chance of the game and  maybe their third chance after scoring 2. So that  
could be the only reason that we would say, okay,  a point is good to take, but for the rest, I think  
for everything else, I'm not happy with the 2-2.  I wasn't happy at all being 2-1 down at halftime.  
That didn't reflect, in my opinion, the first  half at all. But yeah, it's the thing of football,  
if you can see the set piece, things can change  quite quickly. I know in another interview, you've  
said that there's one player in particular who's  pretty down in the dressing room, but I'm guessing  
that's Darwin with the chance that he had. What  was your view of that chance? What could he have  
done better? Because it's easy for us to sit here  and say he could have dinked it, but he could  
have dinked it over Remy Martinez, but he came  sprawling at his feet later on as well. So what  
is it that you need to see? Now, what I saw was an  unbelievable pass from Conor Bradley. And what a  
power run from Dominic Sobersly, who made, in my  opinion, the perfect choice to square it, because  
from a 1v1 to the goalkeeper, he made it an open  goal chance. Yeah, and then Darwin was, of course,  
it was not the best leg, no, he's right footed, of  course, but it was still a big chance. And yeah,  
very unlucky. And I was hoping that he could  have got another one. because a player like him  
probably wouldn't miss two chances in a row and  he was very close afterwards when he went towards  
Martinez again. But yeah, Martinez made a great  sliding tackle to win the ball. I think we were  
all disappointed, but it's normal that a player  that missed a chance like this is always a bit  
more disappointed than the rest. Just check on Con  Bradley. How serious do you think being with his  
initial? Yeah, it was difficult, but if he felt  some he felt a bit when he when he made a sprint,  
he tried to continue, but had to go out all the  times with injuries. I always say if a player  
wants to go out himself, that's not a promising  sign. So that will probably lead to the fact that  
he's for 99. 9% sure not available for City.  And I didn't expect him to get Newcastle as  
well. And then we have to see if it's one, two  weeks or if it's going to be even longer. Does  
every team naturally have a little bit of a dip  in a season? Do you feel like that's what you're  
having at the moment? Is that a natural thing?  We have a dip, why? Just in terms of results,  
in terms of performance. It's hard to be brilliant  in a season, but does every team naturally have  
a little bit of a. . . I think every game has  its own story. I think in terms of performance,  
we weren't brilliant at all at Everton. But for  obvious reasons, we were very unlucky to lose  
over there. I'm sorry, it felt like losing, but it  was a draw, to come away with a draw over there.  
Today, I liked our performance a lot, much, much,  much more than I liked our performance against  
Wolves, from what I liked the most, playing  the ball, bringing the ball out from the back,  
creating chances. So no, I don't feel like that  at all. I think if you go away at Villa, that's  
always a difficult fixture. If you start the  season, you know, oh, Villa, that's a difficult  
one. Oh, City away, that's a difficult one. Yeah.  So performance-wise, not a dip at all today,  
in my opinion, but you might disagree. And  what we must not do, and we've done that a  
bit too often now, is that we don't get what  we deserve. And if you look at all the chances,  
if you put them in a row from us and from them, I  think it's clear which team should have won this  
game. And we must not make a habit out of that,  because it happened a bit too much now. And still,  
we are eight points clear with Arsenal, a game  in hand. So, I mean, the golden assist tonight,  
I mean, it's just, it's his figures  are off for scout. He really feels like  
he's on that mission every time. It's just  remarkable. Yeah, yeah, yeah. Yeah, he is.  
But not only him. I think I couldn't have asked  more today from all the players. They've worked so  
incredibly hard in the fixture list like we have  with so many games to be played, too difficult  
away games at Everton and here, emotional games  as well, because not only the quality you face,  
you also play against the crowds because they are  really helpful at Everton and here again as well.  
So, but Oh, yeah, great goal, although  Jot deserves a lot of compliments for  
that goal as well. And the second one, yeah,  was maybe a bit lucky because Kurt deflected,  
but we were there so many times in that period of  time that it felt to me that we definitely served  
that 2-2 at that moment. Yeah, Carly, could you  just explain the formation today with Curtis and  
Dominic? It seems slightly different. Why did  you do it and did you think it worked? Nah.  
Result-wise, going 2-1 in at halftime, you  could say it didn't work. Performance-wise,  
it worked really, really, really well, because we  totally not deserve to go 2-1 down at halftime,  
again, in my opinion. The reason why we did this  is that Lucio played three games in seven days.  
I played him at the Plymouth because I knew I had  Cody, so I could switch them around if needed. But  
then Goldy got injured in Everton because you  got a big knock. And all of a sudden you have  
only one winger left. So that's why for today  we felt this could work. And I think it did if  
you look at the amount of chances we created and  how we played the game. But yeah, result-wise,  
you never know if you would have done differently  what would have happened. But it wasn't smart to  
play Lucio 90 minutes again. The same way I had  to take out Jot and Trent, both coming back from  
injuries. Jod hasn't played for four or five  months. It's his second start now after four  
or five months. So, yeah, you have to take care  of them, especially in a period of time where you  
play so many games. Well done. Thank you. Thank  you. See you tomorrow. Oh, yeah. 10 to 12 hours.
title: Arne Slot post-match press conference | Aston Villa 2-2 Liverpool
